composition.story: A cell about to divide has already copied its DNA. Step through mitosis: chromosomes condense, spindle fibres attach, chromosomes line up, then anaphase splits every sister pair. Each pole receives one full set, so two identical cells form. Switch organism to see the counts change.

aha.observation: Anaphase splits every sister pair, so the chromosome count briefly doubles (46 to 92) and each pole gets an identical full set of 46.

controls.label: Organism (sets chromosome number)
controls.presentation: Changes every chromosome count in the readouts

states.label: Interphase
states.sentence: Before dividing, the cell copies its DNA. Each of the 46 chromosomes now has two identical sister chromatids.
states.why: Copying first guarantees each daughter can receive a full set.

states.label: Prophase
states.sentence: Chromosomes condense into visible X shapes. Centrosomes move apart and begin building the spindle.
states.why: Compact chromosomes can be moved without tangling or breaking.

states.label: Prometaphase
states.sentence: The nuclear envelope breaks down. Spindle fibres reach in and attach to each chromosome at its centromere.
states.why: Attachment gives every chromosome a handle for being pulled.

states.label: Metaphase
states.sentence: All 46 chromosomes line up along the cell equator, with sister chromatids facing opposite poles.
states.why: Lining up ensures each pole can receive exactly one chromatid of every pair.

states.label: Anaphase
states.sentence: The links break and every sister pair separates. Each chromatid, now its own chromosome, is pulled toward an opposite pole.
states.why: Splitting every pair gives each pole an identical full set: 46 each.

states.label: Telophase
states.sentence: Two nuclear envelopes re-form around the two chromosome sets. The spindle disassembles and chromosomes loosen.
states.why: Each set is now enclosed in its own nucleus.

states.label: Cytokinesis
states.sentence: The membrane pinches at the furrow and the cytoplasm divides, leaving two genetically identical daughter cells.
states.why: Cytoplasm division finishes the split: one cell becomes two.

2.reason: The stepper is learner-driven with no timer, so anaphase holds until Next is pressed. Its sentence, why text and readouts (46 to 92, 0 pairs) all state the aha.

3.reason: The organism select swaps the variant, changing every count (46/92 versus 8/16) in the sentences and readouts. The step control changes the active regions and readouts.

4.reason: The picture, ghost, callout and readout bind to state.active, previous.active, state.calloutRegion, state.sentence and state.readouts. Each calloutRegion id exists in the regions list and the links reference declared regions.

7.reason: Each state activates 3-4 regions with one callout and 4 compact readouts. This is a detailed scene, but it does not exceed the mitosis density ceiling.
